jobs.title: Associate Account Manager (US Students) at AMBOSS
jobs.description: Employer: AMBOSS Expires: 11/03/2026 Location: New York (hybrid) We seek a motivated Associate Account Manager to join our dynamic US Roadshow Team at AMBOSS! About AMBOSSAMBOSS is the copilot for medical professionals, empowering them to provide the best possible care through our learning and clinical decision support tool. Our team brings together care, innovative thinking, and cutting-edge AI medical technology. Our founders launched AMBOSS in 2012 with the goal of creating a tool they wished they had during medical school and clinical practice. Since then, we've grown to over 600 employees and are active in over 180 countries - primarily in Germany and the US. Our offices are located in Berlin, Cologne, New York, Cagliari and Cape Town.Want to learn more about our culture? Watch our video to explore what makes us unique. Why can this position be exciting for you?As an Associate Account Manager, you will play a key role in bringing healthcare education to students. You will support the planning, organization, and execution of events and discount opportunities for US medical students, aimed at expanding AMBOSS’s presence in the market.You'll be the one making our demo events run smoothly, even if you're not the one on stage. Bringing engaging AMBOSS demo events to life, fostering meaningful connections with students, and managing all logistical, strategic, and organizational aspects—from outreach, event planning, to follow-up sales—end to end. You will be pivotal in helping students prepare efficiently for their exams and navigate the journey to their degree with ease.The ideal candidate is enthusiastic about shaping the future of medical education, enjoys, and thrives in a fast-paced environment. You will:Build and maintain a network of student leads to support US Roadshow activities, fostering both new and existing relationships (conducting email marketing campaigns and desk research) Coordinate virtual school visits and on-site demonstrations by converting student leads into event organizersStrategize, plan and execute events, workshops, and webinars to introduce AMBOSS to US medical students in their first couple years of studyingBuild connections with brand rep med students over email Utilize a data-driven and analytical approach to optimize user and revenue growthCollaborate closely with teams including B2B, Marketing, and Clinicians, to spearhead unified strategies to capture the US market You bring:Ideally 1-2 years of experience in Sales, Business Development, Account Management, Customer Success, or related rolesExcellent verbal and written communication skills in English with storytelling Strong analytical skills: ability to methodically collect and interpret qualitative and quantitative data in order to make informed decisions and optimize sales strategies.Familiarity with software tools (e.g., HubSpot, Looker/Metabase, Asana, Google Sheets) is a plus You enjoy:Working across teams, asking questions, and picking up the nuances of each project as you goBringing order to the chaos, whether that's planning an event or coordinating a projectKeeping an eye on the details while juggling multiple priorities as things change quickly CompensationThe salary range for this role is $55,000-$60,000 USD per year, and where you land in that range depends on your experience and the impact you'll bring to the role. Work AuthorizationCandidates must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. We are not able to sponsor work visas for this role. Benefits🌴 Rest & Time Off (22 paid vacation days, AMBOSS holiday, personal purpose day and more)🏃 Health, Fitness & Mobility (Medical, dental and retirement plans; fitness subscription..)🥙Food & Office Comfort (Daily breakfast in the New York office, work remotely from 4 other office locations…)Check out the full list of benefits below:https://go.amboss.com/the-amboss-prescription-nycWe believe that diversity is a powerful driver of innovation and progress. That’s why we are committed to fostering an inclusive, respectful, and supportive environment where everyone—regardless of gender, age, ethnic or cultural background, religion, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity—is valued and given equal opportunity to thrive. We warmly welcome people of all backgrounds to help us fulfil our mission: empowering all medical professionals to provide the best possible care 🩺Even if you don’t meet every single point in the job description, we still encourage you to apply. We’d love to hear from you!

jobs.title: SAT Math Instructor at CodeHeroAcademy - OYA
jobs.description: Employer: CodeHeroAcademy - OYA Expires: 11/04/2026 SAT Math Instructor – Small Group Teaching | $25/hr | In-Person, Alpharetta, GAAbout UsCode Hero Academy - OYA SAT is a local SAT prep program in Alpharetta that believes every student learns best when they feel seen, heard, and supported. We teach in small groups so each student gets real individual attention, and we pair great teaching with a practice and progress-tracking platform that helps students improve steadily.The RoleWe're looking for a math instructor who connects with students as much as with the material. You'll lead small-group SAT Math sessions, keep every student engaged, and use our platform to shape each lesson around what your students need most.What You'll DoTeach SAT Math concepts and strategies to small groups of high school students.Keep every student involved, making sure each one feels their questions and challenges are understood and addressed.Notice when a student is stuck, even when they don't say so, and adjust your approach in the moment.Use our online platform to assign practice, build well-balanced quizzes and practice exams, and track each student's progress.Review progress data to plan upcoming sessions and choose the material that will help the group most.Adapt lesson plans as students grow, pushing those who are ready and supporting those who need more time.What We're Looking ForStrong command of high school math (algebra, geometry, data analysis, and advanced math topics on the SAT).A genuine knack for connecting with teens and making them feel valued and confident.Patience, attentiveness, and the ability to read a room.Comfort with technology and willingness to learn a new teaching platform.An organized planner who can also think on their feet.Prior teaching or tutoring experience is a plus, but not required.Great Fit ForCollege students and recent grads in math, engineering, or education; current or retired teachers; and anyone who loves helping students reach their goals.DetailsPay: $25/hourLocation: In-person, Alpharetta, GA(Occasionally Online) Schedule: weekday evenings and/or weekend mornings/afternoons, Minimum 4 hours per weekStart date: ImmediateTo ApplySend your résumé and a few sentences about a time you helped a student who was struggling to naga@codeheroacademy.com. Applicants who mention a specific example will be prioritized.

jobs.title: Lead Teacher at Seamen's Society for Children and Families
jobs.description: Employer: Seamen's Society for Children and Families Expires: 11/04/2026 Lead TeacherLocation: Staten Island, NYDescriptionThe Organization:Founded in 1846 to care for the children of sailors in the Port of New York, Seamen's Society for Children and Families ("Seamen’s Society”) was one of the first organizations in the US to care for abandoned children in family settings, rather than institutions. Today, Seamen's Society is a comprehensive $28 million nonprofit organization that offers foster care and adoption services, mental and behavioral health care services, prevention/family stabilization services, domestic violence intervention services, a health home care management program, education financial support, a childcare center, and a youth tutoring program. The agency's 200+ professionals serve over 1,250 children and over 500 families in New York City. Programs are conducted in a trauma-informed, caring manner that understands and embraces the diversity of the communities served by the organization.Role: Lead TeacherDepartment: Child Care CenterReports to: Education DirectorLocation: Staten Island, NY (on-site)Compensation: $31.11 per hourEmployment Type: Full TimeJob Summary:The Lead Teacher is responsible for general administrative duties as assigned, for supervision of subordinate staff, and for planning, preparing, and implementing daily activities, monitoring children’s progress, and maintenance of related records for assigned classroom. The Lead Teacher promotes the center’s philosophy and educational objectives.Duties and Responsibilities:· Supervise the planning and execution of a program to provide day care for children which takes into account the educational, social, developmental and health needs of the group, as well as that of the individual child.· Take responsibility for keeping equipment and material accessible and in good condition to encourage maximum constructive use by the children.· Take responsibility for removing or reporting any damaged or hazardous equipment to the director or other designated person so that necessary action may be taken.· Take responsibility for planning and supervising an appropriate arrangement of his/her own classroom furniture designed to promote optimal program functioning.· Share In the overall planning for the best use of shared space In relation to the total center program.· Plan the use of community resources to enrich the educational content of the children's program.· Develop a program of sound educational goals appropriate to the age and developmental level of children that will enable them to make the most of future educational opportunities.Promoting the professional growth of classroom associates· Share with classroom associates their mutual knowledge and understanding of the sponsoring agency and the community that their center serves.· Take responsibility for the professional growth and development of the classroom associates through regularly scheduled individual and classroom group conferences based on daily observation of the associates' performance within the group and their applications of new skills as acquired through training and experience.· In cooperation with the director, assist in the annual evaluation of the job performance of the classroom associates.· Take responsibility for equitable sharing among all classroom personnel relating to all areas of the program.Promoting sound parent relationships· Developing an appropriate plan by which information concerning the children and program can be shared with the parent, the teacher, and associates.· Attend and participate in group parent meetings.· Respect the confidential nature of all information about parents and children.Maintaining objective staff relationships· Maintaining good working relationships and objective attitudes with other staff members,Conducting regular group conferences· Assuming responsibility for planning and conducting regular group conferences with classroom associates, encouraging their attendance and participation in workshops and conferences designed to further their professional growth. ·Cooperating in self-evaluation· Assuming responsibility for discussing his or her own professional performance objectively in regularly scheduled supervisory conferences with the director. Using these conferences as a source of information and professional guidance.Record writing· Writing, keeping, using, and sharing with appropriate staff members such as are required and necessary for the effective administration of the center, the development of the program, work with the individual child, students, and volunteers.Accepting administrative responsibilities· Accepting responsibility when required for fulfilling the overall administrative function in the director's absence.Other related duties, as assigned, consistent with the above.RequirementsSkills, Knowledge, and Abilities:· Supports the professional growth of colleagues by sharing materials and information and providing helpful feedback and encouragement· Excellent oral and communication skills· Strong teaching abilities· AdaptableQualifications/Requirements:· At least a bachelor’s degree in early childhood education and valid certification by the State Education Department· Valid driver’s license preferred· Bilingual Preferred

jobs.title: School Psychologist at Brockport Central School District
jobs.description: Employer: Brockport Central School District Expires: 11/04/2026 Position: School PsychologistLocation: Barclay SchoolRequired Certification: School PsychologistStart Date: August 31, 2026 Position Overview: We are seeking a dedicated and passionate School Psychologist to join our district. The School Psychologist supports the academic, social-emotional, and behavioral success of students by providing specialized services that include assessment, intervention, consultation, and collaboration with educators, families, and community partners. This role ensures that all students have access to a safe, supportive learning environment aligned with state and federal regulations.ResponsibilitiesAssessment & EvaluationConduct comprehensive psychological and educational evaluations to identify learning, behavioral, and emotional needs.Participate in the development and review of Individualized Education Programs (IEPs).Interpret assessment data and communicate results clearly to families, staff, and multidisciplinary teams.Intervention & SupportProvide individual and group counseling aligned with student IEPs or general education support services.Develop and implement evidence-based behavioral, academic, and mental health interventions.Support crisis prevention and response, including risk assessments and safety planning.Consultation & CollaborationPartner with teachers, administrators, and parents to improve student learning and well-being.Provide recommendations for classroom strategies, behavior supports, and instructional modifications.Participate in Student Support Teams, Response to Intervention (RTI) processes, and other collaborative problem-solving structures.Compliance & DocumentationMaintain accurate and timely documentation in accordance with district policies and state and federal laws (IDEA, Section 504, FERPA).Assist in monitoring the implementation and effectiveness of IEP services.School Climate & PreventionContribute to initiatives that promote positive school climate, social-emotional learning, and student resilience.Provide staff professional development on topics such as behavior management, mental health, and trauma-informed practices.Professional Development:Participates in ongoing professional development opportunities to stay current with educational trends, teaching methodologies, and curriculum advancements. This includes attending workshops, seminars and professional meetings such as faculty and department/grade level meetings.Collaborates with fellow teachers and staff to share best practices and enhance the overall learning experience for students.Other:Performs other related tasks as assigned by the Principal, Assistant Principal and other central office administrators as designated by the Superintendent.The above description is illustrative of tasks and responsibilities. It is not meant to be all inclusive of every task or responsibility.Qualifications:Bachelor's degree and NYS Certification in School Psychology.Knowledge of assessment tools, special education laws, and evidence-based intervention practices.Experience working in a K–12 educational setting.Strong communication, collaboration, and problem-solving skills.Patience, flexibility, and a genuine passion for working with children.Training in crisis intervention or restorative practices, preferred but not required

jobs.title: English Teaching Fellow with Masters Degree at The Lawrenceville School
jobs.description: Employer: The Lawrenceville School Expires: 11/04/2026 The Lawrenceville School, an independent boarding and day school located in central New Jersey, seeks dynamic individuals to join our community as a member of the Independent School Teaching Residency (ISTR) program, a two-year teaching fellowship offered in conjunction with the University of Pennsylvania Graduate School of Education (PennGSE), beginning in June 2027. We are now accepting applications for our two-year teaching fellowship program for 2027-2028 in English. ISTR Fellows join their departments at Lawrenceville as fully engaged members of the faculty, teaching their own classes from the start. Fellows will fulfill co-curricular responsibilities (in athletics, performing arts, or publications) and residential duties, including being a member of a House team, chaperoning student events, and advising a group of students in year two. Fellows are paired with a mentor teacher in their discipline who offers support and coaching through regular classroom observations and ongoing conversations about life at Lawrenceville. Regular meetings with the cohort of eight fellows provide collegiality and a strong peer group of early career educators. Teaching fellows are an integral part of a vibrant campus life. Our community lives, works, and eats together, all in enticing proximity to the variety of attractions in Philadelphia and New York. Teaching fellows are required to live in school housing (basic utilities included). They are provided three meals per day in the school dining center and have access to athletic facilities. If hired by Lawrenceville, fellows join their cohort at PennGSE, where they complete a rigorous two year course of study led by PennGSE professors and academic leaders from other boarding schools in pursuit of a Masters of Education from PennGSE. Throughout the year, fellows participate in regular distance learning sessions and gather in person four times–in June, October, January and April–on the UPenn campus in Philadelphia and at various host school locations around New England. Upon completion of the two year fellowship, recent graduates have found desirable teaching and coaching opportunities at both boarding and day schools across the country (including Lawrenceville), as well as have gone on to pursue additional advanced degrees or consultant work. The ideal candidate values hard work, learning and growth as an early career educator, and wants to collaborate to build community, connection and belonging for the students and faculty at Lawrenceville. Essential Responsibilities Teaching (two different preparations/courses)In year one, two sections in Fall term and three sections in the Winter and SpringIn year two, four sections in Fall term and in either Winter or Spring, three in the other ResidentialSupervise a student dormitory as a member of a duty team one night a week from 6:00 - 11:30 pm.Participate in Saturday programming as scheduled by the School.Provide weekend chaperone coverage up to twice per term.In addition, in year two, serve as an academic advisor to a group of six to eight students.Live on campus with a cohort of other fellows and participate in the residential life of the School Co-CurricularCoach at least one season of interscholastic athleticsLead/Co-lead one additional term of co-curricular activity (athletic, performing arts, community service, student publications, experiential learning)Other duties as assignedRequirementsA Bachelor's degree in a relevant fieldRelevant experience working with young peopleRelevant experience in an area of co-curricular school lifeComfort working in a fast-paced, demanding academic environmentThe desire to engage in the life of a boarding school communityEffective written and verbal communication skillsStrong time management and organizational skillsA growth mindsetWhen completing the application, please submit the following to Lawrenceville’s employment portal. We will not review incomplete applications.ResumeCover letterCollege transcript (can be unofficial)Three letters of recommendation (two must be academic references, and one should be a work-related reference). Letters of recommendation can be submitted via email to professionalreferences@lawrenceville.org References should be received by November 5th and be sent to professionalreferences@lawrenceville.org. Please instruct the person providing the reference to put the applicant's name and position they are applying for (eg: History Teaching Fellow) in the subject line of the email. Applications are due October 31st, 2026Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. without sponsorship. We do not provide visa sponsorship for this role. For finalists, on campus interviews will be held between November 10th and November 17th. The Lawrenceville School will arrange transportation to and from campus as well as lodging during the interview. Interviews take place over the course of an afternoon/evening and the following day. Work Characteristics and Physical Demands: The work environment characteristics and physical demands described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.Physical demands are in excess of those for sedentary work. Must be able to remain on their feet for extended periods of time, go up and down flights of steps, as well as stoop, kneel, crouch, and lift.Routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, fax machines, etc.Must be capable of using visual display terminal with continuous wrist movement on a keyboardRequired to stand for long periods of timeRequired to talk, hear, walk, use hands to finger, handle or feel and reach with hands and armsMust be able to lift up to 25lbs. without assistanceAbility to see with normal parameters.Operates in a professional work environmentWill work outside of normal working hoursAdditional informationWorking at Lawrenceville Overview of ISTR at Lawrenceville Class Schedule The Lawrenceville School is a diverse and inclusive community and makes all employment decisions without regard for an individual’s race, creed, color, religion, national origin, nationality, sex, pregnancy, affectional or sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, veteran status, physical or mental disability (including AIDS and HIV related illness), genetic information, refusal to provide genetic information, refusal to submit to genetic testing, ancestry, familial status, marital status, domestic partnership status, civil union status, atypical cellular or blood trait, military service, application for military service, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. The Lawrenceville School will also provide reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals in accordance with applicable law. The Lawrenceville School conducts pre-employment screening for all positions which includes a criminal background check, verification of work history, academic credentials, licenses, and certifications. Employment is contingent upon successful completion of the background check. Eligible employees receive a competitive benefits package that includes health insurance coverage, paid leave and retirement plan options, and many other valuable programs. SalaryThe annual salary range for this residential position is $25,000.00 - $27,000.00, plus a $5,000.00 stipend. Additionally, The Lawrenceville School pays approximately 80% of fellows' graduate school tuition.

jobs.description: Employer: The Lawrenceville School Expires: 11/04/2026 The Lawrenceville School, an independent boarding and day school located in central New Jersey, seeks dynamic individuals to join our community as a member of the Independent School Teaching Residency (ISTR) program, a two-year teaching fellowship offered in conjunction with the University of Pennsylvania Graduate School of Education (PennGSE), beginning in June 2027. We are now accepting applications for our two-year teaching fellowship program for 2027-2028 in History (a background in World or US history is required). ISTR Fellows join their departments at Lawrenceville as fully engaged members of the faculty, teaching their own classes from the start. Fellows will fulfill co-curricular responsibilities (in athletics, performing arts, or publications) and residential duties, including being a member of a House team, chaperoning student events, and advising a group of students in year two. jobs.description: Employer: Martin County Schools (NC) Expires: 11/04/2026 Martin County Schools is currently accepting applications for a variety of Teacher positions. See our website for our current vacancy list.These are 10-month positions, and the salary is based on the state salary scale for teachers, plus local supplement (paid half in November and half in April).Candidates must have or be immediately eligible for a North Carolina Professional Educator's License in the area of interest. Interested individuals without this license should visit the links below for more information regarding the alternative licensure process. (All licenses require the candidate to have earned at least a Bachelor's Degree.)Residency Model License Pathways (from dpi.nc.gov)List of Approved Educator Preparation Programs (from dpi.nc.gov)----------------------------------------------------------------------------------MAJOR FUNCTION: Management of Instructional Time The teacher has materials, supplies, and equipment for each lesson ready at the start of the lesson or instructional activity; gets the class started quickly; gets students on task quickly at the beginning of each lesson; maintains a high level of student time-on-task. MAJOR FUNCTION: Management of Student Behavior The teacher has established a set of rules and procedures that govern the handling of routine administrative matters; has established a set of rules and procedures that govern student verbal participation and talk during different types of activities—whole-class instruction, small group instruction, etc.; has established a set of rules and procedures that govern student movement in the classroom during different types of instructional and non-instructional activities; frequently monitors the behavior of all students during whole-class, small group, and seat work activities and during transitions between instructional activities; stops inappropriate behavior promptly and consistently, yet maintains the dignity of the student. MAJOR FUNCTION: Instructional Presentation The teacher begins lesson or instructional activity with a review of previous materials; introduces the lesson or instructional activity and specific learning objectives when appropriate; speaks fluently and precisely; presents the lesson or instructional activity using concepts and language understandable to the students; provides relevant examples and demonstrations to illustrate concepts and skills; assigns tasks that students handle with a high rate of success; asks appropriate levels of questions that students handle with a high rate of success; conducts lesson or instructional activity at a brisk pace, slowing presentations when necessary for student understanding but avoiding slowdowns; makes transitions between lessons and between instructional activities within lessons efficiently and smoothly; makes sure that the assignment is clear; summarizes the main point(s) of the lesson at the end of the lesson or instructional activity. MAJOR FUNCTION: Instructional Monitoring of Student PerformanceThe teacher maintains clear, firm and reasonable work standards and due dates; circulates during class work to check all students’ performance; routinely uses oral, written, and other work products to check student progress; poses questions clearly and one at a time. MAJOR FUNCTION: Instructional FeedbackThe teacher provides feedback on the correctness or incorrectness of in-class work to encourage student growth; regularly provides prompt feedback on assigned out-of-class work; affirms a correct oral response appropriately, and moves on; provides sustaining feedback after an incorrect response or no response by probing, repeating the question, giving a clue, or allowing more time. MAJOR FUNCTION: Facilitating InstructionThe teacher has an instructional plan which is compatible with the school and system-wide curricular goals; uses diagnostic information obtained from tests and other assessment procedures to develop and revise objectives and/or tasks; maintains accurate records to document student performance; has instructional plan that matches/aligns objectives, learning strategies, assessment and student needs at the appropriate level of difficulty; uses available human and material resources to support the instructional program. MAJOR FUNCTION: Interacting Within the Educational EnvironmentThe teacher treats all students in a fair and equitable manner; interacts effectively with students, co-workers, parents, and community. MAJOR FUNCTION: Performing Non-Instructional DutiesThe teacher carries out non-instructional duties as assigned and/or as need is perceived; adheres to established laws, policies, rules, and regulations; follows a plan for professional development and demonstrates evidence of growth. Performs other related work as required.----------------------------------------------------------------------------------Please direct any specific licensure or employment questions to hr@martin.k12.nc.us.

jobs.title: Founding Executive Director — San Francisco, California at Youth RISE Foundation
jobs.description: Employer: Youth RISE Foundation Expires: 11/04/2026 Youth RISE Foundation, Inc.Location: San Francisco, CaliforniaPosition: Founding Executive DirectorOrganization: Youth RISE FoundationEmployment Type: Founding Leadership OpportunityBuild Something That Does Not Exist Yet.Youth RISE Foundation is seeking an exceptional leader to become the Founding Executive Director for San Francisco, California.This is not a traditional Executive Director position.You will not inherit an established office, existing staff, local programs, or a decades-old reputation. Instead, you will have the opportunity to help build the Youth RISE presence in San Francisco from the ground up.San Francisco will serve as Youth RISE Foundation's Innovation & Opportunity Hub—a place where bold ideas, community partnerships, education, workforce development, leadership, and opportunity come together to help young people build stronger futures.We are not looking for someone to simply manage what already exists.We are looking for someone willing to build it. About Youth RISE FoundationYouth RISE Foundation is a national nonprofit organization dedicated to empowering young people through:ResourcesInspirationServiceEmpowermentOur mission is centered on expanding opportunity for young people and supporting pathways to education, leadership, career development, mentorship, community engagement, and long-term success.As Youth RISE expands nationally, we are launching founding offices across seven major American cities.Seven Cities. Seven Founding Leaders. One National Mission.The Founding Executive Director for San Francisco will become one of the leaders responsible for writing the first chapter of Youth RISE in their community. The OpportunityThe Founding Executive Director is the senior local executive responsible for establishing, launching, and leading the Youth RISE Foundation presence in San Francisco.You will have meaningful autonomy to develop local strategy and build relationships while operating within the Foundation's national mission, policies, standards, financial controls, and organizational framework.You will be expected to:Understand the San Francisco community before designing solutionsConduct a comprehensive community needs assessmentIdentify gaps affecting young people and emerging adultsBuild relationships with community leaders and organizationsDevelop strategic partnershipsIdentify universities and educational institutions for collaborationBuild a local funding and development pipelineScout potential office and program locationsDevelop locally relevant programsRecruit and help build the founding teamEstablish volunteer and community networksBuild the Youth RISE brand and reputation locallyLaunch programming that meets national standardsLead local operations, partnerships, fundraising, and strategyProduce measurable outcomes for young peopleYou will be building the foundation upon which future employees, volunteers, students, donors, mentors, partners, and community members will stand. What You Will BuildYour work will move through six founding areas:1. DiscoverBefore building, you will listen.You will research:Youth demographics and community needsEducational institutions and universitiesExisting youth-serving organizationsService gaps and unmet needsWorkforce and career opportunitiesFunding and philanthropy opportunitiesCommunity organizations and trusted leadersPotential university chapters and partnershipsKey Deliverable:A credible San Francisco Community Needs Assessment and Local Strategic Plan. 2. ScoutYou will help determine what a Youth RISE presence should look like in San Francisco.This includes:Identifying potential office locationsExploring shared and partner spacesEvaluating program and meeting facilitiesConsidering transportation and accessibilityIdentifying university proximity and collaboration opportunitiesAssessing operational needs and costsWe believe the goal is not to build the largest footprint.The goal is to build the right footprint. 3. BuildYou will build the local organization.This includes:Community relationshipsStrategic partnershipsVolunteer recruitmentStaff recruitmentUniversity relationshipsCommunity visibilityLocal systemsPrograms designed around actual community needsA sustainable annual operating planYou will help establish the culture, credibility, relationships, and systems that future generations of Youth RISE leaders will inherit. 4. FundA mission requires resources.The Founding Executive Director will work closely with Youth RISE national leadership and shared-services functions to help develop a sustainable local funding strategy.This may include:Foundation grantsCorporate partnershipsSponsorshipsGovernment opportunitiesIndividual donorsMajor giftsCommunity fundraisingIn-kind partnershipsYou will not be expected to build funding infrastructure alone.However, you will be expected to lead the local effort and build meaningful relationships that support the long-term sustainability of the San Francisco office. 5. OperateOnce the office launches, you will be responsible for ensuring it functions effectively.This includes leadership and accountability for:Staff leadershipProgram implementationCommunity relationshipsBudget managementOffice operationsRisk managementCompliancePerformance reportingOrganizational cultureStrategic executionA successful office should eventually be capable of operating through systems and leadership—not solely through one person. 6. ServeAbove everything else, this role exists to serve young people.The Founding Executive Director should consistently ask:"Does this help us create greater opportunity for the young people we serve?"If the answer is no, we reconsider the decision.This is not a role built around titles.It is a role built around impact. What Success Looks LikeWithin the First 90 DaysYou will be expected to work toward:A written community needs assessmentA local strategic planA partnership pipelineA funding pipelineIdentified priority partnersA preliminary office and infrastructure strategyA clear launch planWithin the First 6 MonthsThe San Francisco office should be progressing toward:Operational readinessEstablished partnershipsApproved programmingInitial fundingCommunity engagementLaunch preparation and/or program deliveryWithin the First 9 MonthsThe office should be working toward:A functioning local teamActive partnershipsProgram deliverySustainable operating systemsNational reporting and accountabilityBy the 12-Month ReviewSuccess will be evaluated through areas including:Community impactPartnershipsProgram effectivenessFunding developmentTeam developmentOrganizational cultureOperationsCommunity reputationMeasurable outcomes for young people Who We Are Looking ForWe are looking for a builder.Someone who can walk into a community, listen before speaking, identify opportunities, and bring people together around meaningful work.You may come from:Nonprofit leadershipYouth developmentHigher educationGovernmentCommunity organizingWorkforce developmentPhilanthropySocial servicesHealthcareEducationPublic affairsBusinessEntrepreneurshipCommunity developmentWe are less interested in whether your résumé follows a traditional path than whether you can demonstrate:LeadershipPeople have trusted you to lead difficult and meaningful work.JudgmentYou can make thoughtful decisions, even when information is incomplete.CompassionYou treat people with dignity and respect.ExecutionYou have actually built things—not simply talked about building them.IntegrityYou handle responsibility, relationships, resources, and mistakes with honesty.ResilienceYou understand that meaningful work is difficult, and you know how to continue moving forward. Experience We ValueWe welcome candidates with experience working alongside communities and populations that may include:Young people experiencing homelessnessFoster and former foster youthLGBTQIA+ youth and communitiesImmigrant and newcomer communitiesFirst-generation college studentsYoung people experiencing educational barriersYoung people experiencing economic instabilityJustice-impacted individualsUnderserved communitiesCommunities historically excluded from opportunityYouth RISE evaluates candidates based on their experience, qualifications, leadership capability, and ability to perform the role. The Ideal Candidate Can Answer:What have you built that still exists today?How have you earned trust in a community?When were you wrong about what a community needed, and what did you do next?What meaningful partnership have you built from the ground up?What funding relationship have you helped develop?How have you helped change the trajectory of a young person or community?How do you turn vision into execution?How do you build something that can continue beyond you? Reporting StructureThe Founding Executive Director is part of the Youth RISE Foundation national leadership structure.The Founding Executive Director will work closely with and receive support from the national executive office, including functions responsible for:OperationsFinanceHuman ResourcesProgramsLearning & DevelopmentPublic AffairsExecutive LeadershipThe San Francisco office remains part of one national organization and operates within the Foundation's established governance, financial, programmatic, compliance, and organizational standards. What Youth RISE ProvidesYouth RISE Foundation provides the national framework, mission, vision, organizational standards, and infrastructure to support founding leaders.You will have access to:National executive leadershipOrganizational guidanceEstablished policies and standardsProgram frameworksHuman Resources infrastructureCompliance and screening processesFinancial controls and supportProfessional developmentNational shared servicesCross-city collaborationA national network of founding leadersYou will not be expected to build alone.But you will be expected to lead. This Role Is for You If...You see a problem and immediately begin thinking about how to solve it.You believe young people deserve access to more opportunity.You know how to build relationships across different communities and sectors.You can speak with a university leader, corporate executive, community organizer, donor, and young person—and treat every person with the same dignity.You understand that leadership is not about being the most important person in the room.It is about making the room better because you were there.You are comfortable with ambiguity.You are not waiting for a perfect system before beginning meaningful work.You want the opportunity to build something that may outlast your own tenure. This Is Not a Traditional Executive RoleWe want to be transparent.A founding opportunity requires a different kind of leader.This is not an established office with:A large existing staffA mature local donor baseLongstanding community relationshipsFully developed local programsAn established office infrastructureYou will be helping create those things.That means there will be difficult days.There will be unanswered emails.There will be partnerships that do not work out.There will be funding opportunities that do not materialize.There will be problems nobody anticipated.That is what founding means.You are there to help solve problems that do not have answers yet. jobs.title: AmeriCorps Math Fellow - Small Group Instruction at Blueprint Schools Network
jobs.description: Employer: Blueprint Schools Network Expires: 11/04/2026 ​ AmeriCorps Math FellowOrganization: Blueprint Schools NetworkProgram: AmeriCorps Math Fellows ProgramTerm of Service: One Academic School Year Position Location(s): Balsz School District - Phoenix, ArizonaAbout Blueprint Schools Network & The RoleAt Blueprint Schools Network, we believe that every student possesses incredible potential that deserves to be fully realized through high-quality, personalized instruction. As an AmeriCorps Math Fellow, you won’t just support students—you’ll help expand access to high-quality math instruction for young people who deserve every opportunity to succeed. Along the way, you’ll build the skills, experience, and confidence to become an exceptional educator and community leader.As a Fellow, you will deliver intensive, small-group math instruction during the school day, working directly with students to build their confidence, strengthen their foundational math skills, and help them reach their full potential. You will receive structured onboarding, regular 1-on-1 coaching, collaborative lesson planning, and whole-group professional development throughout the program year.This is practice-based learning at its best: you grow as an educator in real time, backed by a supportive professional network.Real service. Real students. Real results.Why This Role MattersThe opportunity gap is real—and Fellows help close it.Far too many students—disproportionately those from historically under-resourced communities—move through school without receiving the rigorous, personalized math support they need to build lasting confidence and academic momentum. The effects compound: students who fall behind early are less likely to access advanced coursework, post-secondary opportunities, and economic mobility.Blueprint Math Fellows serve at exactly this inflection point. By providing daily, intensive small-group instruction, Fellows accelerate learning, rebuild academic confidence, and help students access the full promise of their education. The impact isn't abstract—it is measurable, and it belongs to you.Term Options & National Service BenefitsAmeriCorps service comes with a bi-weekly living allowance rather than a salary or hourly wage over the term of service (academic school year). Within each region, the final living allowance falls within a specific band determined by the local school/program day schedule and average daily on-site service hours.Living stipend band ranges (for school day schedules of 6 hours or more) per region for 2026-2027 School Year are:• Arizona: $21,000 to $24,000* prorated based on start date. *Living Stipend: Living allowances are paid out in equal bi-weekly installments across the active term of service. Total stipend amounts may be adjusted for members starting after the official program launch date based on remaining pay periods. In addition to the living stipend, Blueprint AmeriCorps Math Fellows that meet AmeriCorps service hour requirements and remain in good standing are eligible for an end-of-term living allowance balance aligned with their AmeriCorps slot.• Three-Quarter Time (1,200 service hours): $1,000• Half-Time (900 service hours): $500Note: The majority of service hours are completed through direct tutoring services provided to students during the school day. Remaining service hours are earned through professional development and volunteer activities.**End-of-Term Living Allowance Balance: End-of-term living allowance balance disbursement upon completing all required service hours while remaining in good standing. Full details regarding Blueprint’s living stipend and End of Year Completion Bonus are provided to candidates during the recruitment process. Additional Member Benefits• Eli Segal AmeriCorps Education Award: Upon successful completion of your term, members may earn an Education Award usable toward existing qualified student loans or future higher education tuition and expenses.Segal AmeriCorps Education Award Amounts (subject to start date and completion of service hours)Full-Time - service hours required 1,700 by end of program year - Segal Education Award: $7,395.00Three-Quarter Time - service hours required 1,200 by end of program year - Segal Education Award: $5,176.50Half-Time - service hours required 900 by end of program year - Segal Education Award: $3,697.50Reduced Half-Time - service hours required 675 by end of program year - Segal Education Award: $2,817.14Quarter-Time - service hours required 450 by end of program year - Segal Education Award: $1,956.35Note: An individual may earn up to the value of two full-time education awards in their lifetime across all national service terms. Under current federal law, the Segal Education Award is considered taxable income in the calendar year in which it is used/redeemed. • Healthcare Coverage: Full-time members are provided medical, dental, and vision with 100% of the individual-level premium paid by Blueprint. Cost-sharing plans are available to add dependents. • SNAP Benefits: AmeriCorps members are eligible to apply for Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program benefits to help offset monthly food costs through their state programs. Eligibility is determined by individual state rules.• Loan Forbearance & Interest Accrual Repayment: Eligible federal student loans may be placed in forbearance during service, with interest paid off by AmeriCorps upon successful term completion.• Built-in Professional Time: Paid time designated specifically for daily prep/planning and up to 72 hours of professional growth and 1-on-1 instructional coaching.Blueprint Schools Network BenefitsOur Benefits & Employee Well-being• Planning and Preparation: Daily planning and preparation built into your schedule• 30 minute duty free lunch• Sick leave and personal leave• One-on-One coaching and ongoing feedback.• Real-world experience valued across education and mission-driven careers • Fellows enrolled in Blueprint’s medical plan have access to All One Health Assistance Program: Access confidential, 24/7/365 support at no cost to you or your household members. Services include professional mental health counseling, financial and legal and work-life. Phone, app, or portal.• Ongoing Well-being Support: Take advantage of monthly interactive EAP orientation sessions designed to help you navigate and maximize your mental health, financial, legal, and work-life benefits. • Telehealth & Virtual Care: Access board-certified primary care doctors, dermatologists, and behavioral health therapists via video or phone through MDLIVE and Talkspace. • Pre-Tax Commuter Savings: Save up to 30% on public transit, parking, and vanpooling expenses with convenient payroll deduction accounts. Key Responsibilities (AmeriCorps Member Service Activities)During your term of service, you will:• Deliver High-Impact Instruction: Lead daily, small-group math instruction during the school day for small cohorts of students.• Data-Driven Support: Track student progress and adapt instructional approaches in real time using assessment data.• Build Meaningful Relationships: Foster strong, trusting relationships with students to build academic confidence, engagement, and a positive mindset toward math.• Collaborate with Educators: Partner closely with classroom teachers, school administrators, and fellow AmeriCorps members to align tutoring with classroom instruction.• Engage in Professional Growth: Participate in daily planning sessions, 1-on-1 coaching, and structured professional development (up to 72 hours per year).• Maintain Service Commitments: Complete required service hours over the course of the school year.From Tutor to Teacher: Explore Your PathwayWhether you are exploring a career in teaching, planning to get certified, or simply driven to do meaningful work, the Math Fellow role gives you the foundation to move forward with purpose.Through our "Tutor to Teacher" path, you will gain essential professional skills like communication, adaptability, and problem-solving. As you consider your next steps, Blueprint connects Fellows with partner organizations and pathways into teaching, formal teacher certification, and graduate study.Qualifications & Eligibility RequirementsAmeriCorps Eligibility Requirements:• Be at least 18 years of age at the start of service.• Be a U.S. citizen, U.S. national, or lawful permanent resident.• Satisfy the National Service Criminal History Check requirements.Role Qualifications:• Education: Current enrollment in a degree program, prior enrollment, or completion of an Associate’s or Bachelor’s degree.• Language Skills: Proficiency in English required; Spanish language skills are a plus.• Core Competencies: Passion for educational equity, strong communication skills, empathy, adaptability, and a desire to work directly with students.• Commitment: Ability to commit to the full school-year term of service and reliably commute to assigned school placement and commit to assigned schedule.• Satisfy Blueprint and local school/district background screening requirementsApply TodayThis is more than a role—it’s a chance to build a career rooted in purpose, impact, and growth.Apply today and start making a difference.This program is available to all, without discrimination on the basis of race, color, sex, sexual orientation, pregnancy, religion, age, national origin, genetic information, disability, military status, familial status, political affiliation, or any other characteristic protected by law. Blueprint Schools Network is an equal opportunity organization committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion.This material is based upon work supported by AmeriCorps under Grant No. 26NDFMA001. Program services are funded in part by AmeriCorps and local matching public funds. ​

APPLY TO FIND OUT MORE!Pay Range: $20-$28 per hourExpected Hours: 20-30 hours per weekClient Locations: Colorado: Aurora, Brighton, Broomfield, Centennial, Denver, Lakewood, Littleton, Longmont, Parker, ThorntonClients Availability: Weekdays - Daytime, Afternoons & Evenings. The BT or RBT will work directly under the supervision of a BCBA (Board Certified Behavior Analyst) to provide high-quality ABA therapy (Applied Behavior Analysis) to children with autism and other developmental disabilities. The ideal candidate will have a genuine passion for working with children and a strong interest in behavioral therapy. We hire BTs and RBTs with the intention that our hires will transition into more senior roles at Horizons, including full time and leadership RBT roles, BCBA roles ultimately Clinical Director and managerial roles.Why Work with Us?We started Horizons ABA because we wanted to build an ABA company with a unique, therapist-centric culture; together with our clinical leadership we have created an environment that is growth-oriented, professional, and fulfilling. Here is how:I. Compensation: We believe our team deserves to be compensated well for their efforts, contributions, and achievements. We offer competitive compensation and benefits and a variety of regular bonuses based on achievable milestones. We want you to hit them!II. Training and Career Development: We offer comprehensive training and mentorship opportunities for our RBTs. Whether our RBTs are interested in full time technician leadership positions or in pursuing a masters degree and a BCBA role, we support them. From financial stipends to specialized training programs, Horizons will help you reach your career goals. Join us and start building a rewarding career!III. Leadership and Engagement: Our clinical leadership is world-class and provides direct guidance and mentorship to our RBTs. In addition, the two founders are mission-driven and intimately involved in day-to-day operations and work with all of our staff directly. At our company everyone has a voice and if you have feedback or suggestions, we want to hear about it!IV. Work / Life Balance: At Horizons, we believe in work-life balance and we help our RBTs find the right balance of Scheduling that best suits their interests, availability, and needs. From current in-home opportunities where we strive to minimize our team’s commutes to upcoming clinic-based roles in 2025, we work with you to find the perfect balance for you!V. Reduced Administrative Burden: We utilize innovative software, AI tools, and efficient workflows to reduce our RBTs’ tedious administrative work and provide them with more time to focus on their clinical passions and build their behavioral therapy skills.VI. Our Culture: We diligently built our company from scratch to create an inviting and therapist-centric culture. We lead with empathy. Character, ethics, and attitude are as important to us as intellect, ambition and work ethic. Making sure our team members feel supported and heard is core to our identity. We foster community through exciting team outings and social events. We want you to enjoy being a part of our team!Key Responsibilities IncludeDirect TherapyImplement individualized ABA treatment plans developed by BCBAs.Provide 1:1 therapy sessions to clients in settings including homes, schools, and community locations.Utilize ABA techniques such as discrete trial training, natural environment teaching, and behavior modification strategies.Data Collection and ReportingAccurately collect and record data on client behavior and progress during each session.Maintain detailed session notes and progress reports.Communicate client progress and any concerns to the supervising BCBA.Client and Family InteractionBuild positive and supportive relationships with clients and their families.Assist in training parents and caregivers to implement ABA strategies in the home.Provide guidance and support to families to help generalize skills learned in therapy.Collaboration and TeamworkParticipate in team meetings and supervision sessions with BCBAs.Collaborate with other RBTs and therapists to ensure consistent implementation of treatment plans.Contribute to a positive and productive team environment.QualificationsHigh school diploma or equivalent; Bachelor’s in Psychology, Education, or related field preferred.Current certification as an RBT or willingness to obtain RBT certification.Experience working with individuals with ASD or other developmental disabilities is preferred.Experience working with children is a big plus.Strong understanding of or interest in behavioral therapy principles and technique.Excellent communication and interpersonal skillsAbility to follow detailed treatment plans and instructions.Valid driver's license and reliable transportation (if applicable).And most importantly – kindness, integrity, empathy and a genuine desire to help others.WHAT ARE WE LOOKING FOR WHEN WE HIREOur team is what makes our company stand out in an industry with many different types of providers. We understand that it takes a special type of person to succeed in this role, and we are committed to only hiring the best of the best clinicians to foster a high-quality, collaborative environment. Horizons ABA is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.Apply now to become part of an exceptional team transforming lives through ABA Therapy!

jobs.title: Part-Time After-School Entrepreneurship Lead Coach at Kidfoundry
jobs.description: Employer: Kidfoundry Expires: 11/04/2026 After-School Program Entrepreneurship Primary Coach —Employer: KidFoundry LLC Location: Multiple Public Schools Houston, Texas — on-site Position type: Part-time, school-term position Student group: Grades 2–5 Schedule: Typically 2-4 Days of the week, approximately 3:00–4:30 p.m Program dates: 01/05/2027- 05/28/2027* ( Can be selected for the next term based on performance)Compensation: $25–$40 per hour based on experience and expertise. Reports to: KidFoundry Program Director About KidFoundry KidFoundry helps children develop an entrepreneurial mindset through hands-on projects, games, teamwork, and presentations. Our elementary-age programs introduce students to identifying problems, developing product ideas, creating prototypes, understanding customers, setting prices, marketing, and pitching. Along the way, students practice creativity, communication, problem-solving, and collaboration. Our goal is to help children turn their ideas into something they can explain, develop, and share with confidence. About the role We are seeking a dependable, engaging instructor to deliver KidFoundry’s existing entrepreneurship curriculum as an after-school program at multiple elementary schools around Houston. This opportunity is well suited to a candidate who enjoys working with children and has an interest in business, education, entrepreneurship, or youth development. Selected candidates will be given priority for various holiday camp positions- summer, spring, thanksgiving and winter. You will lead interactive lessons and guide students through projects using KidFoundry’s lesson plans and activities. You will also manage classroom routines, supervise students, and help create a welcoming and fun environment where children feel comfortable asking questions, trying ideas, and learning from mistakes. KidFoundry will provide curriculum training, lesson plans, program materials, and ongoing guidance. You are not expected to design a new curriculum. What you will do ● Review the provided lesson plan before each session and prepare the materials needed. ● Arrive in time to set up the classroom and receive students according to the school’s procedures. ● Teach entrepreneurship concepts through short explanations, relatable examples, games, and hands-on activities. ● Guide students as they brainstorm ideas, build prototypes, explore pricing and marketing, and prepare simple pitches. ● Facilitate teamwork, discussions, and presentations so every student has opportunities to participate. ● Establish clear routines and use calm, positive strategies to address distractions, disagreements, and transitions. ● Adapt explanations and provide support for students with different ages, abilities, and confidence levels while maintaining the lesson’s learning goals. ● Maintain accurate attendance and supervise students throughout the session and authorized dismissal. ● Follow school and KidFoundry procedures for safety, emergencies, student privacy, and professional conduct. ● Organize supplies, clean up the learning space, and provide a brief session update to the Program Director. ● Communicate promptly about supply needs, student concerns, incidents, or scheduling problems. ● Weekly camp briefing to the Camp Director in person or remote. Required qualifications ● Direct experience working with children through camp counseling, tutoring, coaching, classroom assistance, after-school programs, or structured youth volunteering. ● Ability to lead activities, explain instructions clearly, and maintain a respectful, organized learning environment. ● Interest in entrepreneurship and willingness to learn and accurately deliver KidFoundry’s curriculum. ● Strong communication, organization, and follow-through. ● Consistent availability for the advertised schedule and commitment for the full program session. ● Reliable transportation to and from the schools ● Willingness to complete required background screening, school clearance, and program training before working with students. Experience gained through volunteering is welcome. Please describe the children’s ages, your responsibilities, and whether you led groups independently. Preferred qualifications ● Current enrollment in a college or university program/ or a graduate degree, particularly business, entrepreneurship, marketing, education, psychology, communications, or a related field. ● Experience leading groups of elementary-age children. ● Familiarity with positive classroom management and hands-on learning. ● Coursework or practical experience involving product development, marketing, budgeting, or presentations. ● Current CPR/first-aid certification. What we provide ● Paid curriculum training and onboarding. ● Ready-to-use lesson plans, activities, and program materials. ● Ongoing support and feedback from KidFoundry’s leadership. ● Practical experience in teaching, facilitation, youth development, and entrepreneurship education. ● A consistent after-school schedule. How to apply Submit your résumé and a short statement to hr@Kidfoundry.com explaining: 1. Why are you interested in the program coach position at KidFoundry. 2. Your experience working with children, including their ages and any group leadership responsibilities. 3. Your availability during the program dates. 4. Two Professional references and permission to contact them. Please also include two professional references and permission to contact them. For student applicants, references may include a teacher, professor, volunteer coordinator, or supervisor familiar with your reliability and work. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to an interview and then a brief teaching demonstration using a prompt supplied by KidFoundry. If selected, paid training will be held during Thanksgiving break 23rd November- 27th November 2026* in person during our camp. Application deadline: 30th October 2026 KidFoundry welcomes applicants from different academic backgrounds who can bring patience, creativity, reliability, and a commitment to helping children learn. * dates are subject to change

jobs.title: Literacy Tutor at OnYourMark Education
jobs.description: Employer: OnYourMark Education Expires: 11/04/2026 Who We AreOnYourMark Education is a high dosage virtual tutoring service providing individualized virtual literacy instruction grounded in the science of reading. We partner with schools as a supplement to the literacy instruction already in place to ensure students get the foundational reading skills they need to excel! Why We ExistOnYourMark exists to ensure that the students we serve have a strong foundation to become thriving readers. We also believe that spreading an understanding of the science of how children learn to read can be transformative for tutors, teachers, children, and families. Getting foundational literacy skills right early will support children to read on grade level and diminish the need for schools to remediate at their current levels. Why ApplyWhen you become an OnYourMark Literacy Tutor, you commit to supporting students in becoming lifelong readers with the foundational reading skills to tackle future school and life challenges. Becoming an OnYourMark Literacy Tutor is right for you if you are invested in having an impact on the lives of young people, are committed to learning new skills, and are inspired by being a part of eradicating educational inequities. Who Should ApplyBecoming an OnYourMark Literacy Tutor is perfect for college students, college-aged students taking gap years, recent high school and college graduates, current tutors, and retired and part-time educators. It is ideal for those who love working with children and are interested in learning more about a career in education. Successfully building tutoring skills will open up possibilities to continue as a tutor, tutor coach, and build a resume that opens doors for future opportunities in schools as teachers, leaders, and beyond. Position OverviewOnYourMark Literacy Tutors provide virtual high-dosage tutoring to Kindergarten through 8th-grade students grounded in the science of reading. Tutors learn how to teach an explicit phonics curriculum to support the development of foundational reading skills. Literacy Tutors will support students through one-on-one or small groups in a virtual setting. This individualized approach will increase the speed at which students develop as readers by third grade, the year that research shows students must master these skills to engage in increasingly complex texts as they progress in school and life. Upon successful completion of onboarding and training requirements, tutors will enter the Tutoring Pool. During this time, tutors will sign up for available one-off tutoring sessions in need of substitute coverage until they are offered a schedule. Schedule assignments are based on school schedule needs and tutor availability. OnYourMark shall use its best efforts to provide a placement for tutors to provide tutoring services, but shall not guarantee a specific placement. Your CommitmentsParticipate in paid virtual pre-service training: approximately 22 hours for new tutors or 4 hours for most returning tutors. Click here to view our Time Commitment Guide.Attend and complete ongoing professional development learning sessions and scheduled coaching, individualized or small group sessions, as assigned during active tutoring contract. Manage a caseload of students by building strong relationships, collecting data regarding progress, preparing lesson materials, and supporting students in their prescribed learning sequence.Track student reading skill progress over the course of tutoring sessions via scheduled progress monitoring assessment and student survey completions.Commit to a tutoring schedule aligned with the academic calendar year. Programming typically runs from September through June, though hours and schedules can vary considerably within that window. There is typically a 3-4 week break in tutoring around the holidays December and January, aligned with typical school breaks. Exact dates may vary by school. Limited summer hours may be available in July.To effectively support our program, tutors must be available during the hours when OnYourMark offers tutoring services.Learn from literacy experts and deepen your understanding of how children learn to read, grounded in the science of reading.Inspire a love of reading and learning in the students you serve. Additional requirementsBe at least 18 years of ageHold a high school diploma or equivalent, GEDReside within the contiguous U.S., Hawaii, or Alaska and be authorized to work in the U.S. Tutors must satisfy an online comprehensive background check and, if applicable, complete the appropriate fingerprinting requirements outlined by each school partner assignment.Have a computer with a Chrome browser and a working microphone &video. Your internet connection must support a minimum of 25 megabytes per second for download and 25 megabytes per second for upload. CompensationLiteracy Tutors are compensated at a rate of $17.50/hour for non-student-facing activities including training, tutor development, administrative tasks, and in scope tutoring lesson preparation. Early Literacy Tutors are also compensated at a rate of $18.25/hour for facilitating tutoring sessions and other student-facing activities. Tutors also have the opportunity to substitute for additional one-off sessions as available for additional compensation.

Maintains budget records and files. Receives and processes accounts receivable, receives periodic printouts of financial performance and prepares summary reports. Assists in the budget development process by gathering and compiling information required for budget development. Develops and maintains a working knowledge of special terminology related to the function to which assigned. May takes and transcribe dictation, or compose complex documents from rough drafts or verbal instructions using modern word processing software. Independently composes and distributes common correspondence and routine forms. Receives telephone calls, provides information as appropriate, resolves certain matters, or routes calls to other officials as necessary. Arranges meetings as directed. Prepares schedules and informs participants, confirming dates and times. Makes travel arrangements as directed.Attends meetings as assigned to represent the department, sometimes in place of the department head. Maintains committee records, assists in the preparation of departmental reports by gathering and summarizing information from a variety of sources. Maintains confidentiality.Performs other duties as assigned that support the overall objective of the position. QualificationsKnowledge and SkillsRequires a thorough knowledge of office practices, procedures and equipment, including filing systems, receptionist and telephone techniques, and letter and report writing. Requires a working knowledge of those activities associated with accounting, budget and payroll transaction processing, and statistical record keeping. Requires a working knowledge of personal computer based software programs that support this level of work, including but not limited to word processing, spreadsheet, presentation graphics, and data entry onto custom data bases. Requires thorough knowledge of proper English usage, grammar, spelling, punctuation and mathematics skills. Must be skilled in using various standard office machines, including personal computers with word processing, database, desktop publishing, and spreadsheet applications. AbilitiesRequires the ability to independently perform all of the duties of the position efficiently and effectively. Must be able to perform office and secretarial work with speed and accuracy. Must be able to learn, interpret, explain and apply knowledge of District and department organization, operations, programs, functions and special department terminology to relieve an administrator or program director of a variety of administrative detail. jobs.description: Employer: University of Nevada, Las Vegas - Center for Academic Enrichment & Outreach Expires: 11/04/2026 This is a temporary, part-time (38 hours/week) position with benefits. The incumbent will have a workspace off-campus at 1455 E Tropicana Avenue, Suite 325 and Suite 380.General DescriptionThis position works under the general direction of the Director for Adult Educational Services (AES) and assists with the oversight and administration of federal TRIO adult-level programs. The primary goal of this position is to support program participants in planning for and pursuing a college education. The position provides academically at-risk and under-resourced adults, as well as veterans, service members, and family members, with opportunities to obtain a high school equivalency certificate, continue or resume postsecondary education, and improve retention and graduation outcomes. The position develops and coordinates all counseling and advising aspects of the program, including academic advising and course selection, study skills, personal concerns, career exploration and preparation, ACT/SAT preparation, financial aid information, institutional admissions requirements, and assistance with financial aid applications and the college admissions process. The Coordinator fosters and strengthens partner and community involvement in preparing students for college, supports student recruitment and retention, conceptualizes new programming to enhances participants’ academic success, and assists in developing and implementing program goals, operating procedures, programmatic initiatives, outcome assessments, and grant-writing activities. This position is exempt from overtime. Job Functions• Assistance with college applications, finding scholarships, and completing financial aid applications• Informing participants about careers options including workforce development• Providing academic advising and assessing individual learning styles• Visit schools and community organizations to disseminate information about the EOC program, recruit and serve eligible participants to meet grant numbers and objectives. • Provide academic and personal advising to support participant growth and educational goals. • Guide participants through the high school equivalency (HSE), college application and career exploration processes during individual and group advising sessions.• Discussing financial literacy• Conducting virtual presentations• Documenting services and maintaining federally-mandated participant records• Learning and adhering to project guidelines and meeting assigned objectives• Assisting with special projects*Training and computer equipment to work at school sites and remotely will be provided. QualificationsEducation: Minimum--Bachelor's degree from a regionally accredited university; Preferred--Major in Education or related fieldRequirements: Ability to pass a federal and state background check, ability to drive and maintain a valid driver's license, excellent verbal and written communication skills in English; excellent interpersonal skills and attention to detail; advanced computer skills (Google Docs, Canvas, MS Word, Excel, Power Point, and Adobe Suite). Preferred: Excellent interpersonal skills; advanced analytical skills and attention to detail; advanced computer skills (Google Docs, MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Adobe Suite); Preferred--Advising and counseling secondary students, working with low-income and first generation students, experience in/working knowledge of CCSD, and experience with remote services and content delivery through Canvas and Google platforms. Ability to speak Spanish is also preferred. If you have any questions, please email a resume with a letter of interest to cicely.morgan@unlv.edu.

This is a hands-on role at the center of daily school operations — you'll keep things running smoothly behind the scenes while building real relationships with families, staff, and students.What you'll do- Assist the Director with day-to-day operational and administrative tasks.- Serve as the first point of contact at the front desk for families, visitors, and staff.- Help with school opening and/or closing procedures as needed.- Maintain accurate, organized records and ensure information stays current.- Communicate clearly and warmly with families and staff to support a positive school experience.- Coordinate teacher and classroom needs — supplies, scheduling, and ongoing communication.- Assist with family tours, enrollment, orientation, and admissions.- Monitor compliance with local, state, and federal early education standards.- Help sustain a positive, inclusive school culture that values diversity and collaboration.- Step in to support classrooms or other operational needs when the situation calls for it.About you- AA or Bachelor's Degree in Early Childhood Education, Child Development, or a related field preferred.- At least 2 years of experience in an administrative role.- Strong organizational, communication, and multitasking skills.- CPR and First Aid Certification, or willingness to obtain.- Friendly and proactive — comfortable working independently and as part of a team.Compensation and BenefitsCompetitive salary commensurate with experience and education, with potential for additional responsibilities. Benefits package may include health, dental, and vision insurance and paid time off, subject to school policy.Franklin Academy integrates service learning, creative development, a whole-child philosophy, and intentional leadership formation. Each child is nurtured to discover their strengths, think critically, and contribute positively to their community.
